newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Ssangyong seeks more foreign capital.
newsitem.headline: Ssangyong seeks more foreign capital.

text.p: South Korea's Ssangyong Motor Co on Friday announced its net loss had sharply widened in 1996 and said it would seek to attract more foreign shareholders as part of efforts to raise more funds while reducing its cost burden.
A company spokesman said its after-tax net loss had risen to 228.49 billion won in 1996 from the previous year's 126.23 billion won loss.
"Our business performance in 1996 suffered from increased financial costs resulting from huge capital investments implemented in the past," Cho said.

Cho also said the company, a unit of the Ssangyong Group, would allow foreign companies to take up to 49 percent of its paid-in capital, compared with the 10 percent ceiling that applied by the end of 1996.

"In order to reduce outside borrowing, we have no choice but to raise funds without interest. We will promote to attract more foreign capital investors in that sense," Ssangyong's president Lee Chong-gyu told reporters.
As of the end of 1996, Germany's Daimler-Benz AG held a 2.6 percent stake in Ssangyong, which makes four-wheel drive utility vehicles and commercial vehicles.
